theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Energy is the dominant theme by rank, breadth (0.786, the widest participation), and durability_bar (0.68). The trend-gate leg (validated risk control) currently holds it eligible. Crowding is flagged (z=1.04, crowded=true), so this is a size-down caution only — it caps exposure but does not justify fading the leader. I lean with the confirmed leadership, not against it.
evidence: eligible=true under the validated absolute-trend gate
theses.dissent: Crowding + a robust 0.0298 one-way move over the prior window (r10) can mark a near-term top; if breadth stalls while price stays high, the leadership is at risk of a shake-out that the trend gate is designed to exit, and the crowded cohort could fall as one.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO breaks below its own 20-day average while breadth drops under 0.5 before the 20-day check-by.

theses.subject: Pipelines & Midstream
theses.thesis: Pipelines share the same Energy leadership narrative but with lower crowding (z=0.51, crowded=false) and the highest durability_bar in the sector (0.68, tied with producers). Hurst_tag=trend and breadth=0.375 suggest a quieter, trend-sturdier expression of the energy complex than the crowded producer leg. Not scorable (no ETF proxy), so I mark conviction low and lean directionally only.
theses.dissent: Unscorable (no proxy) means the call cannot be graded cleanly; midstream often trades like a bond proxy and may lag the commodity-price-led move in producers, so the total-return case is thinner than the headline energy trade.

falsifier.text: If the broad Energy complex (XEG.TO) drops more than 8% from its current level before the 20-day check-by, the midstream trend leg is no longer supported.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold is the rotation challenger (rank=2, score=1.11) and is eligible under the trend gate, with manageable crowding (z=0.2). It is NOT a confirmed handoff — the champ-vs-challenger margin (0.502) is still wide and rotation is not directional (directional=false). I lean modestly with the challenger as a second leg rather than a fade of Oil, because the leadership has not actually rotated.
theses.dissent: Breadth is weak (0.267) and durability_bar is only 0.48 — this is a narrow, fragile move concentrated in a few names; if gold has not confirmed a breakout in price, the miners can mean-revert hard and the challenger status disappears.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO falls more than 6% from current level while XEG.TO stays flat or up, before the 20-day check-by.
